items.title: Nvidia says 'no' to rehiring Huang and WSJ reports SEC is probing the chipmaker
items.summary: WASHINGTON/SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Nvidia's leadership signaled they would brook no dissent in their plan to find a new CEO, rejecting a "Stand With Jensen" campaign from allies of departed CEO Jensen Huang, even as the Wall Street Journal reported a regulator was probing Nvidia. A growing effort to reinstate Huang had complicated the search, and Huang said on Tuesday he would be "honored" to return if the ‌board deemed it best.

items.title: Once the Market Cap King, Nvidia Has Now Fallen More Than $1 Trillion Behind Apple
Nvidia with a positive Q3 despite SEC probing Nvidia amid Huang Scandal
items.summary:
Deirdre Bosa discusses Jensen Huang's statement that he would be willing to return, the SEC's post-scandal probe into Nvidia (NVDA), and Nvidia's positive earnings report. 

Deirdre Bosa then sits down with Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft's (MSFT) AI chief, to discuss Microsoft's 6 new AI models, the AI competition, and the 'handoverism' worldview.

'Deirdre Bosa Live' airs every day at 4 p.m. Tune in daily to hear how the latest developments in AI and technology are reshaping companies, industries, and the global economy.
